Provide funding to make venues accessible to visitors and performers, We want the UK Government to provide funding to make venues fully accessible to visitors and performers. This should include making stages, toilets, bars and viewing areas fully accessible to disabled people., We need equality for disabled performers and visitors to venues. 

Being a disabled music fan, producer & DJ in the local scene, I wanted to go to more gigs to hear my music live - this was when I realised how inaccessible the majority of venues are. I noticed even further when I started to organise & perform at shows - I quickly realised I couldn't get on stage and it was a struggle to find a venue that had wheelchair access for disabled audiences and performers.

Seek cross-party agreement on policy and funding for the NHS and social care, We believe that the current Government should not set policy and funding for the NHS and Social Care on its own. I would like to see the Government take a cross-party approach to agree on policy and funding, taking into account all the concerns identified by the NHS, Kings Fund, BMJ and ADSS., It seems clear that the current approach to NHS/social care policy is not working. Over the last ten years policy and decisions have not been made and we can wait no longer. The answer is not blaming efficiency or even increased private sector involvement, it’s just underfunding and an inability to make uncomfortable political decisions. The disagreements within Government just add to inaction and greater suffering and hardship by service users, employees and increasingly the economy.

Immediate action by Government to address crisis in NHS, Address the current bed blocking that is occurring in hospital's by commissioning Under used residential care homes as a temporary measure to relieve the bedblocking.
To give all nurses, doctors and other professional medical staff within the NHS the same pay award granted to MPs this year of £2200, I am becoming more exasperated by the sheer incompetence of the current government to take action to address the ongoing crises with in the NHS due to insufficient beds and staffing. 

They have presided over 12 years of underfunding, neglect and indecision with putting in place a vision to ensure the health service continued to offer improved services.

Make work permits available to anyone who entered the UK legally after 10 years, The Government should make work permits in the short list occupations leading to settlement available to anyone who entered the UK legally and has been residing here from over 10 years. This could be particularly valuable to people who have faced repeated visa curtailment., Many people who entered the UK legally have experienced issues after the Home office curtailed thousands of students visas because of English Language courses.
 
Lack of support and other available options mean many have overstayed without the opportunity to complete their studies.
 
Many of these are skilled people who could fill vacancies in short list occupations.
 
Making them eligible to get a work permit would give them the opportunity to contribute to the UK's economy.

Fair pay for NHS staff to end the strikes and prevent more unnecessary deaths., Please accept the fair pay rises requested by NHS staff so that the workers can provide a safer healthcare system and save lives.

NHS staff chose this job to help people and save lives - stop taking that away from them., The NHS is crumbling due to insufficient funding, unfair pay and substandard working conditions for its staff. This has resulted in severe staff shortages due to poor retention which has led to unnecessary deaths of citizens. Staff continue to feel burnt out from constantly working over-time due to the shortages. Paramedics are unable to reach people in time to save lives. Tax-paying people who would like to fund the NHS are dying outside of hospitals due to staff shortages. This has to stop.

Mandate MPs (and immediate family) cannot use private healthcare, Mandate all MPs and their immediate family members experience the same level of healthcare as the general public by banning the use of private healthcare and queue jumping within the NHS., The NHS is fundamental to the well being of our country. We must encourage our MPs to protect this vital asset. One way to ensure its proper funding is to disallow those whom maintain it (and their immediate families) from queue jumping or resorting to private healthcare. If MPs have to use the NHS as the general public do, perhaps their approach to its funding will improve.

Fund 24/7 pharmacies and 24/6 GP practices to ease pressure on hospitals, Many people with non-life threatening illnesses are approaching A&E for medical attention as there is nowhere else to go. Round the Clock Pharmacies and 24/6 GPs could help reduce the influx of such patients in A&E, and we want the Government to provide the funding to enable this., Some patients just needs to be seen to get medication or analyse symptoms, they do not need the facilities at A&Es. This could either be dealt with by a pharmacist or a GP. Only if the GP or pharmacist cannot be of help should someone need an A&E. We believe 24/7 pharmacies and 24/6 GPs are necessity. Non-life threatening patients can use these services. Over the weekends many patients have no access to pharmacies or a GP.

Seek to commence UK/Australia visa changes on same day as free trade agreement, I want the UK Government to work with the Australian government to ensure that changes to Working Holiday Maker/Youth Mobility schemes, making these available to people aged up to 35, and removing requirements to undertake particular work, to commence on the same date the new FTA comes into force., I'm turning 35 years old and I want to travel to Australia for work and travel but I'm currently too old for the Working Holiday Maker scheme. This new agreement could will grant me the opportunity and I want to ensure I don't miss out due to my age.
 
A lot of people are in the same situation and I believe making the changes happen as soon as the FTA enters into force would be highly appreciated by many British and Australian citizens.

Close down all the bars in the House of Commons, The workplace is no place for alcohol! There have been too many reports of MPs and HoC staff under the influence of alcohol where behaviour appears to have fallen below the standards expected by the public, including allegations of sexual harassment, bullying and assault., While bars and social clubs in most workplaces such as offices, factories, hospitals and police stations have closed, bars in the HoC have remained open. There is no special case for MPs being able to go to bars at wok, especially given the reports of misbehaviour whilst under the influence of alcohol, and the importance of decision making in the HoC. When they drink, individuals are more likely to be impulsive. The area around the HOC has adequate places to drink after the working day if needed.

Require bar/club staff to be trained in dealing with spiking incidents, We believe that bar/club staff should be required to be trained to identify symptoms of spiking and what action to take if they suspect someone has been spiked. This should ensure staff are better able to identify and respond to these situations., Drink and needle spiking is increasing among young people in night clubs and bars. The Government must take action to try and ensure the wellbeing of victims. Drink and needle spiking can have devastating physical or mental health consequences on victims.
 
We believe that training of club/bar staff is necessary to ensure that victims receive the help and support they need to minimise the effects of spiking incidents.

Make it a legal requirement for local authorities to provide public toilets, Public toilets are not just a convenience - they're a necessity. Access to toilets and washing facilities is important for good public health and to prevent the spread of disease., The law currently allows, but does not compel Local Authorities to provide toilets. We want this to change.

Lack of toilets can lead to street fouling; a major public health issue,
toilets in private business premises do not meet everyone's needs.

Age UK says the dearth of public toilets is adding to older people's social isolation because they are reluctant to risk going out without knowing there is a toilet available and that dehydration was an extra hazard.

We want a law requiring Local Authorities to provide and maintain suitable, safe, clean and appropriately located Public Toilets with realistic opening hours.

Offer healthcare workers on tier2 visa ILR after 2 years instead of 5 years, Healthcare workers are meant to have lived in the UK for at least 5 years before they can apply for ILR. With the work they do and the demand for their skills world wide, they deserve to get residency status much quicker. Most healthcare workers are working under extreme pressure in the UK., Many countries offer immediate residency status for occupations that are in high demand or extremely short. The UK has been a destination for most foreign nurses and doctors, it is time for the Government to show they care and also appreciate the workers by making some of the restrictions in terms of residency more favourable. This could also reduce the number of care workers leaving the country for other countries that offer better conditions.

Hold a referendum on re-nationalising all public services, Let the public vote on re-nationalising all public services that have been privatised, or are being contracted out to private companies. This would stop revenue from taxes being diverted to individuals via businesses as profit., The money earned by all skilled and unskilled workers that's paid as tax, is given on the understanding it's invested in our public services. The money should guarantee that these services function to an acceptable standard at all times, and are available to all. However, we believe many services run by the private sector are instead neglected and deprived of funding for frontline services and staff, leaving them barely functioning and inadequately staffed.

Provide online visa application tracking so applicants can check the status, There are huge delays in processing visa applications, and applicants are often left in the dark without knowing the status of their application. There is no online mechanism for checking the visa status, and the response rate to queries is slow and often does not provide useful information., It is unfair to leave applicants knowing nothing about their applications, especially if they apply from inside the UK and cannot leave the country before a decision is made. This uncertainty causes much anxiety and impacts the well-being of applicants and their families. The Government charges huge fees for processing visas, and there is no excuse not to introduce such tracking mechanisms. People need to know their status, so they plan their life and activities.

Fund after school care for all disabled children, Provide funding for after school care for disabled children across the country. This could be done by providing funding for after school activities at schools, or transport to and funding for places at activities or clubs elsewhere.,

Provide food vouchers for disabled children, unable to access their meals.
, We ask the Government to ensure that disabled children who are eligible, but who cannot access their school, still receive their free school meals. This would mean requiring local authorities to put a system in place to provide food vouchers to disabled children who are unable to access their meals., We want to ensure that disabled children are not substantially disadvantaged and can receive the means tested Free School Meal benefit, the same as their non disabled peers can, and to guarantee that their disability does not get in the way of accessing this support.

According to the Equality Act 2010 and Education Act reasonable adjustments should be made. During the pandemic lockdowns, supermarket vouchers were sent out, proving that there is a practical, discreet and inclusive solution.

Overturn the decision to allow use of neonicotinoid pesticides on sugar crops, The decision needs to be reversed. The health of our environment must be put first., Defra has re-authorised the emergency use of thiamethoxam to protect sugar beet crops from the Yellow Virus. However there is widespread evidence of harmful effects of this neonicotinoid on bees and other pollinators, and its use in the European Union is banned for this reason. Bees and other pollinators are vitally important for the UK’s ecosystem, and they are already in decline. The decision needs to be reversed.

Double funding for the NHS, I would like the Government to double funding for the NHS, to enable them to increase facilities and recruit more staff., Because it is too slow to get seen in hospital or by GP and people are dying while waiting for help.

Cut tax on pub beer & increase shop bought alcohol tax to save jobs, By increasing tax on supermarket alcohol and offsetting with tax cuts on pub beer, jobs in hospitality could be saved, additional revenue raised and more NHS and Social Care money raised. Pubs and community resources (e.g. social and sports clubs) could run at profit., Cut tax on pub alcohol, increase tax on supermarket alcohol. Seems obvious.

Require local authorities to offer a hot meal delivery service, Provision of a meals on wheels service is not a statutory service requirement and Local Authorities in England do not have to provide this service. I want the Government to require local authorities to offer a service providing hot food to the oldest and most vulnerable people at home., Warwickshire County Council is to withdraw its Meals on Wheels home delivery service at the end of May. This decision will directly affect hundreds of older and vulnerable people who use this service. This service cut may mean that people can no longer stay at home and will need to move into care, putting extra strain on the NHS and stretched care services, and potentially lead to ill health or death.

Support pubs and breweries by making the draught drink relief 20%, The Government is planning a welcome but inadequate 5% draught drink relief. It is marginal (2-3p a pint). Introducing a 20% discount (8-11p a pint) should help boost the brewing and pub industry amidst the cost of living crisis and recovery from the pandemic, reversing needless decline., Pubs and drinking establishments have been at the heart of Britain's culture for centuries. The pandemic and rise of online and supermarket beer sales has made pubs less competitive for alcohol and yet this undervalues and erodes their social value; their great part in our communities and culture.
 
It is time the Government supported our pubs and brewing heritage and recognised their economic and societal importance with a 20% draught drink relief to help this industry recover and thrive.

Apply to join the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), We are a trading nation that ultimately depends on sales of our goods and services; by joining EFTA the UK can also apply to be party to the EEA (European Economic Area) agreement allowing us completely tariff-free trade with the EU., 1. Opportunity to completely eliminate tariffs with over 430 million customers.
2. It should simplify the Northern Ireland border problem.
3. Help reduce tensions with Scotland improve long term hopes for the continuation of the Union.
4. Help regain our reputation as a stable, English speaking country as a stepping stone into Europe for the rest of the world.

Seek to rejoin the EU Pet Passport scheme, For the UK Government to seek to negotiate re-entry to the EU Pet Passport scheme., We believe arrangements for pets to travel to the EU should not have changed post Brexit. Many UK residents travel to Europe and should not be burdened with new, more costly arrangements.

Grant Home Fee status for all who are in the UK under the BNO visa, British National (Overseas) visa holders in the UK have moved to the UK to settle. Having home fee status for those attending universities makes it easier for them to settle in.,

Require larger changing tables for children with special needs in public toilets, Require venues be more inclusive, by requiring larger changing tables in their toilets, for children who need to be changed/have nappies changed, as many parents of children with special needs need these facilities but cannot use the standard baby change tables that are in most toilets., I have a child with special needs, he is almost 4 and a big boy for his age. When we are out, it is impossible to change his clothes/nappy on the baby change tables and it is unhygienic changing him on the floor.
 
Many children with complex needs wear nappies well into childhood and beyond, so larger changing facilities or extendable tables being available when out and about is essential.

Subsidise school sports kit for girls from lower-income families., We ask the Government to subsidise sports kit, including sports bras, for girls from lower-income families, and to work with schools to ensure sports bras are included on kit lists as standard., Affordable access to sports bras would significantly improve adolescent girls’ experiences of school sports. As the Government’s ‘Sporting Futures’ strategy explicitly acknowledges, sport creates enormous physical and mental health benefits for young people. By failing to support girls with access to the right clothing we are perpetuating the exclusion of girls from sport.

Review of The Road Vehicles Lighting Regulations 1989, The legislation is nearly 35 years old and doesn’t take into account the improvements made with regards to vehicle lighting and no legislation exists for the use of LED technology in a headlight unit built for halogens.,

Grant immediate asylum to "manifestly-well founded" asylum claims in the backlog, Approve all Home Office identified "manifestly-well founded" asylum claims that have been in process for over 12 months. The Government has introduced what it calls a "streamlined asylum processing model" for processing some "manifestly well-founded cases". We want these claims approved immediately., The Home Office has identified a number of countries from which asylum claims can be said to be "manifestly-well founded." It proposes to deal with these by requiring asylum seekers to complete a lengthy, complex form, in English, within 20 days. This is an onerous burden to place on new arrivals, whose first language is unlikely to be English, and for whom it may be difficult to obtain professional help with the form within the 20 days. We believe this will not help reduce the backlog and could lead to additional appeals.

Remove restrictions on additional work by Skilled Worker visa holders, Currently, Skilled Visa holders are only permitted to do additional work in the role for which their visa was granted, or in a shortage occupation. Any additional work, even if it is part-time or freelance, requires their visa to be updated. We believe this restriction is unfair and unnecessary., This restriction limits the opportunities for visa holders to supplement their income and gain valuable experience outside of their primary role. Skilled worker visa holders are already highly qualified and experienced professionals who have been vetted by the UK Government. We believe allowing them to do additional work outside of their primary role, or shortage occupation areas, would not only benefit them but also the UK economy.

Seek full UK membership of the EU Horizon project, I want the Government to seek to fully rejoin the Horizon project as fully paid up members with all the advantages of collaboration with top European scientists this would allow. The current agreement for the UK's association excludes the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund., If the Government does not negotiate and fund full membership of Horizon UK we are concerned this will lead to a brain drain of senior scientists, which could lead to a catastrophic decline in our advances in medicine, life sciences, environmental development etc.

Increase funding for therapies and equipment for disabled children, I want the Government to put more funding into giving disabled children the therapies and equipment they deserve in order to give them the best quality of life., Many families with disabled children will pay privately or approach charities to give their children what they need. This is a necessity for these children to reach their full potential and shouldn't be looked at as an optional extra. More funding will provide more opportunity for these children and enable them to reach their full potential and have the best quality of life.

Review provision of fully accessible toilets in NHS hospitals, I used to work in the NHS as a trainee pharmacist and I'm a double amputee. One of the reasons that I was unable to complete my foundation training year is due to accessibility issues. I graduated with a First Class Master of Pharmacy degree, but I've been forced to leave the pharmacy profession., I would like the Government to review provision of fully accessible toilets in NHS hospitals. Standard wheelchair accessible toilets are not meeting the health and sanitation needs of a wide range of people, particularly those with limb loss or shortened limbs.
 
There needs to be suitable staff disabled toilets in all hospitals as well. Toilets should be maintained regularly and cleaned well too. I can use disabled toilets at public places, public attractions and many more places but I can't use the toilets everywhere in the NHS. There are 14.6 million disabled people in the UK and there's an ageing population, so this needs to be addressed.

Legally require cafes, pubs and restaurants to provide baby changing facilities, We want the Government to amend the Public Health Act 1848, so that private premises such as cafes, pubs and restaurants have to provide baby changing facilities by law. This should be known as “Annie’s Law.”

This is an issue that affects millions of people across the U.K., The idea for “Annie’s Law” arose when our local NCT parents group were visiting a cafe in the Hammersmith area popular with parents and babies. 

We were forced to change our infants on the floor of their bathroom or in our prams, because the business lacked baby changing facilities. The venue said they didn’t provide facilities because it was “expensive and smelly.”

We agreed this was neither safe nor sanitary, so we decided to do something about it by campaigning to change the law.

Invest all revenue from tobacco duties into NHS pulmonary services, The Government receives substantial revenue from duties on cigarettes and tobacco, yet the NHS has a huge backlog of lung healthcare patients. We want the Government to invest all revenue from tobacco duties to NHS pulmonary services.
,  We want all of this revenue to be invested in NHS pulmonary services, to ensure that these services are at an acceptable level.

Keep the bus services running through Rassau and garnlydan, ebbw vale, Stage coach are planning on stopping the X15 bus service through Rassau and Garnlydan and in June/July the fflecsi bus service to Rassau and Garnlydan will also be cancelled, this will leave our residents unable to travel to town, or anywhere., I have no idea what else to do and need the help to keep the service running for the residents of Rassau and Garnlydan

Remove age and time restrictions on working visas for Australian/NZ nationals, The UK's recent trade agreements with Australia and New Zealand include greater access to visas for citizens of these countries., However, these visas will only be available to 18-35 year olds, and will be limited to three years. We want these age limitations and time restrictions to be removed.
 
We believe granting further eligibility for citizens of Australia and New Zealand - by removing age limitations on those eligible to apply for visas and time limitations on said visas - will advance CANZUK relations with our closest partners.

Make it a legal requirement to have bleed control kits in all public places, We want a law put into place that requires bleed control kits in all public places - including businesses, schools, pubs and bars, etc., Having bleed control kits can save a life. I know first-hand the effects knife crime can have and how important a bleed control kit can be.

Remove Nigeria from the Healthcare UK Red List, Nigerians provide vital services across all sectors in the UK. As part of Commowealth family it is disheartening that contributions of Nigerians to the UK healthcare sector has not been appreciated. Considering current NHS crisis; Nigerians have the youthful population and skills to help our NHS., This will ensure the skilled staff needed to reduce the shortage of trained caregivers in the UK healthcare ecosystem thereby reducing the numbers of elderly patients staying in hospitals longer than required as there are not enough caregivers to care for them in the comfort of their homes. Care homes are constantly looking for staff and Nigeria with its younger population can provide the trained staff needed to reduce the immense pressure our beloved NHS is currently facing.

Seek visa-free travel in EU for families of British citizens travelling together, We want the Government to seek changes to current travel agreements with the EU, to allow non-EU and non-UK family members of British citizens to travel with their families/partners without needing a visa, as they could pre-Brexit., Non-EU and non-UK spouses and other family members of British Citizens are struggling to travel with their partners and families to Europe and through Europe because they now require Visas. However, getting a visa is difficult, which can result in loss of flights booked and additional expenses of travelling to further a-field Visa processing centres for appointments as well as paying private visa agencies that are charging exorbitant amounts to help get Visas.

Fund alternative solutions to provide better broadband to poorly connected areas, Having good broadband is vital but fibre cannot reach everyone. This is a major issue - Ofcom says there are over 500k properties that still can't get decent broadband (min 10 Mbps) via landline. 

Funding must be provided to bring alternative broadband solutions to areas where needs are greatest., Project Gigabit aims to provide full fibre broadband to 85% of UK properties by end 2025 at a £5 billion cost, but much is being spent in high population areas with good broadband already. The USO is also no help to many of the 15% of UK homes & businesses left out.

Alternative solutions are low-cost & installable anywhere immediately. EG using 4G to level up all digitally excluded UK premises with life-changing better broadband would only cost £300 per property - just 3% of that £5bn spend.

Protect the NHS and All Healthcare: Require #MasksInHealthcare, We urge the Government to implement a policy requiring mask wearing in all healthcare settings including hospitals, clinics and GP practices for staff, visitors and patients. An FFP2 minimum should be mandated, to protect against infectious diseases, including COVID-19., Vulnerable patients, such as the elderly, individuals with weakened immune systems, and those undergoing treatments, are at higher risk of severe illness or death from infectious diseases.
 
Requiring everyone in healthcare settings to wear masks is a crucial preventive measure to reduce the spread of diseases, including COVID-19, and protect patients from airborne infections.
 
Masks act as a barrier, preventing transmission and safeguarding the health of patients and healthcare workers alike.

Require sanitary bins be provided in men and women's toilets, To make it a requirement of any toilet in public or any business, restaurant etc, for men or women, must have a sanitary bin available. There is a particular issue with the lack of availability of sanitary bins in men's toilets, for people who need to dispose of incontinence pads., Many men suffer from incontinence, including as a result of medical treatment, and need somewhere to dispose of their pads. Currently sanitary bins are often only provided in women's toilets, and even that is not specifically required in law. This really needs to be changed. There are so many men who need this facility.

Run a multiple choice referendum on the UK's relationship with the EU #Brexit, I would like the Government to arrange a multiple choice referendum to run alongside the next general election., Options should include:
 
Apply to rejoin the EU
Do not apply to rejoin the EU
Apply to join the Single Market & the Customs Union (the Norway/Swiss model)
 
We believe there haven't been any real Brexit benefits but the downsides in terms of trade relationships and staff shortages have been all too obvious. There have also been serious problems with the Northern Ireland protocol which have threatened the Good Friday Agreement.
 
Most polls since the UK has left the EU have indicated that support for Brexit has declined. The people of the UK need to determine the direction the country goes in, a referendum is the fairest way to establish this.

Fund fixed wireless broadband setup costs for poorly connected areas, Ofcom says there are over 500k properties unable to get decent broadband (min 10 Mbps) via landline but over 420k of these could get decent broadband via wireless technology like 4G., Already available & well-proven alternative broadband solutions must be funded in areas where needs are greatest.
 
Project Gigabit aims to provide gigabit coverage to 85% of UK properties by end 2025 at a £5 billion cost, but more solutions are needed right now for those left behind.
 
Alternative solutions that are low-cost & installable anywhere already exist, so funding must be increased or redirected to deploy these.
 
Using 4G to level up almost all digitally excluded UK premises with life-changing better broadband in a rapid timeframe could only cost £300 per property or under 3% of that £5bn spend.

Require disabled toilets have changing stations large enough for children/adults, I want the Government to require all disabled toilets have a full-sized changing bed/table/trolley, that is large enough for children or adults, and not just babies., Changing stations in disabled toilets are often inadequate for parents or carers of disabled children or adults.
 
Many disabled children and adults need to be changed, but changing stations in most toilets, including disabled toilets, are often too small.
 
Carers of disabled children or adults are often left with no choice but to change the child or adult they care for on the floor of a disabled toilet, which is often filthy.
 
The lack of facilities for disabled people can lead to isolation.

Launch a public consultation on legal protections for birds of prey, We want the Government to launch a public consultation on legal protections for birds of prey.
 
Numbers of birds of prey in the UK are increasing, which has also led to them killing more small birds, including song birds, field birds and pigeons.
, We want the Government to launch a public consultation to give the public the opportunity to express their views on the legal protections for birds of prey, and whether these are still appropriate giving increasing numbers, and the effect this is having on smaller birds.

Introduce new pay and benefit entitlements for food delivery drivers, The cost of living has increased substantially in recent months, but some food delivery companies have reduced payments for their drivers, and food delivery drivers also have limited entitlements to benefits. Food delivery drivers are important workers and the Government should protect them., To be able to earn a living many food delivery drivers are working 10-14 hours a day. We believe this is unfair.
 
We want the Government to introduce a minimum wage or rate of payment per mile, and also require companies that drivers work for to provide benefits to their staff (such as sick and holiday pay).

Make it a legal requirement for all domestic cats to wear a bell., Reduce the decline in bird populations across the country. A sizeable number of birds are killed by pet cats each year and this would be reduced if those cats wore bells.

Bird poplations have been in dramatic decline in the UK for decades and this measure may help slow the decline., Birds are an essential part of the ecosystem and if the decline in their populations is not halted then we are failing future generations.

Allow Healthcare Workers on skilled worker visas to work for any employer, The Government should allow Healthcare Workers who came to the UK on a Skilled Work or Tier 2 visa to change employers and work for any employer, irrespective of whether they have a sponsorship licence, without needing to update their visa., Some healthcare workers are exploited by employers, or denied their rights to pay and safe working conditions, or threatened with visa sponsorship withdrawal when they raise concerns.
 
These kind of conditions are resulting in workers suffering from mental health conditions, and treatment by some employers can amount to modern slavery, and negatively affect service delivery.

Reinstate carrying forward time left on passports during renewal, We used to get any remaining time left on our passport added to the expiry date of the new passport. We are now losing up to nine months on our passports, depending on when you renew. We believe this is not fair, and want the Government to reinstate the old rules., We are sold a 10 year passport, when in fact we don't get 10 years. Factoring in that the renewal process takes around 10 weeks and you can't travel to many countries without 6 months validity, many passport holders lose around 8 months. It is only right for the customer to get what they pay for.

Increased funding to improve public schools, We want the Government to provide additional funding for public schools to improve the quality of education, facilities and food, so that students attending public schools do not lose out to those attending private schools., It is apparent that students who attend private school often gain advantages that those who attend public school do not. I wish for everyone to have the same opportunities for educational excellence, so everyone can have equal chance to have a bright future and go to college and university if they want to. But in a public school this can be harder to achieve than for someone with a private education. Being able to pay for private education should not allow some students to gain additional advantages.

Evacuate Sudanese nationals whose travel documents are held by the UK Government, Evacuate Sudanese nationals whose travel documents are held in UK Government offices that have been closed due to the current conflict. Some Sudanese nationals have been approved for visas or waiting for an application to be considered, but now can't travel because they do not have their passports., Some of these individuals have been approved for entry into the UK and have the right to escape the ongoing conflict and war in Sudan. However, their inability to retrieve their passports from UK Government offices has left them stranded and unable to leave the country.
 
Some of these individuals are spouses/partners to UK residents. We implore the relevant authorities to take urgent steps to evacuate these individuals from Sudan.

Help nhs Sudanese staff to exit the country, Help nhs staff with visas to return safely to uk, 50% of doctors working in the NHS are from abroad: many are from Sudan. Despite service to the nhs for several years and holding a visa they are not being helped to escape sudan unless uk passport holders. Over 70 doctors are in this position. I urge the UK government to help them return to the UK to their jobs here safely

Fund half price bus and trains fares for 16 and 17 year olds, Currently on most bus and rail services, under 16s pay a cheaper fare than those ages 16 and above. This allows young people to afford public transport more easily, but these reduced fares do not normally cover those aged 16 to 17., 16 and 17 year olds qualify for a much lower minimum wage than those ages 18 and up, but are expected to pay full fares for travel despite this. Allowing young people within this age range to access cheaper public transport could increase the use of public transport overall, and decrease reliance on parents or friends for lifts.

Give students a legal right to access school toilets when they have their period, Bright Futures NE proposes that young people should have a legal right to access school toilets when they have their periods. Young people, when they have their period, should never be refused access to use the toilet., Young people who have periods during school hours are sometimes denied access to toilets. This prevents young people from having a period with dignity, causing shame, embarrassment and preventing them from changing period products. We believe this is inconsistent with the right to dignity and basic human rights - as per the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Bright Futures NE propose young people with periods, by law be given a right to access school toilets.

Amend guidance for PIP claimants on advising the DWP of travel abroad, The PIP handbook says claimants should notify the DWP if they are planning to go abroad for 4 weeks or more, but the guidance on changes of circumstances says "You must contact the PIP enquiry line if [...] you go abroad." This is inconsistent. Both pages should refer to travel of over four weeks., Disabled people should have the same right to travel abroad for holidays, work, family and other reasons as non-disabled people. Travel like this does not change a person's care or mobility needs. Disabled people shouldn't have to inform the DWP of travel abroad lasting under four weeks. People on tax credits only need to notify travel abroad of over 8 weeks. This is less favourable treatment of disabled people and we believe is discriminatory.

Halt 5G technology in the UK to protect health, I'd like the government to remove all 5G masts and stop any further roll-out of 5G technology to protect people and planet., Scientific research on the impact of 5G technology demonstrates potential harm to health. Please refer to the European Union's conclusions on the health impact of 5G:
 
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/RegData/etudes/STUD/2021/690012/EPRS_STU(2021)690012_EN.pdf

Provide free public transport for all UK citizens at the age of 60., In Wales, Scotland and London 60 year olds are given free access to public transport. Those living in England  have to wait until  age 67.  This petition asks that steps are taken to stop this economic discrimination and provide all UK citizens free public transport at the age of 60., To stop English citizens being discriminated against and ensure fair access to free public transport.

Moratorium on release of game birds for shooting to limit spread of bird flu, To help limit the catastrophic spread of avian influenza, call an immediate moratorium on the release of captive bred gamebirds and mallards for shooting in the UK this year. Take a precautionary approach to limit the spread of avian influenza and reduce the risk of new strains of the disease., Every year over 40 million Pheasants and Red-legged Partridges and 2.6 million Mallard ducks are reared in captivity and then released into the UK countryside to be shot for sport.

Since 2021 there have been 10 outbreaks of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) in gamebird rearing premises. One in Scotland, five in England and four in Wales.

Defra’s statistics on HPAI in wild birds show 70 positive tests in Pheasants in 2022 from August to December, with a peak occurring in October.

Make it mandatory that all disabled toilets should be fitted with a bidet, We would like you to make it mandatory that all disabled toilets are fitted with a bidet (wash & dry toilets). , For all businesses/buildings where it is mandatory to provide an accessible toilet it should also be mandatory to provide a bidet within those toilets. This would including pubs, restaurants, leisure facilities, and travel accommodations.
 
We believe would help those individuals that require this service to live a more independent life and not miss out on the things other people participate in without barriers.

Stop schools locking toilets, To enable children in schools the right to access a toilet at any time of the school day.
This should be a basic human right, locking toilets with gates and refusing children access can have awful psychological and physical implications......this has to stop!, To enable children in schools the right to access a toilet at any time of the school day.
This should be a basic human right, locking toilets with gates and refusing children access can have awful psychological and physical implications......this has to stop!

Stop ilegal workers on food delivery companies, Get food delivery companies to stop been the easiest option for ilegal workers, Food delivery companies has become the easiest option for ilegal workers to earn money, this people not only don’t have to the right to work in UK, they also do not pay the lawful taxes.

Allow biometric residence permit (BRP) holders to use eGates at passport control, Although BRPs have chips that can be read by an automatic system, holders cannot enter the UK using eGates. Instead, they must be checked manually at passport control, which can take hours at busy airports. We want the Government to allow BRP holders to use eGates at passport control., Biometric residence permits (BRPs) issued to non-citizen UK residents contain biometric information such as photo and fingerprints, as well as the immigration status.
 
Allowing people who reside in the UK to use eGates could help relieve the pressure at passport control and reduce waiting times.

2% Non Consolidated lump sum to all non Annex 1 staff who are on AFC contracts, To honour the 2% Non Consolidated payment for 2022 - 2023 to all healthcare professionals who are working from agenda for change contracts but are not directly attached to a trust. This includes community nurses and 111 call centre staff., As a community healthcare nurse we wear several different hats. Our training is in forefront of our mind as we are not aware what we will be presented with when going into a patients home. We, as with hospital staff worked with patients throughout the pandemic including when they were at the end of there life. 
We feel the government has forgotten about the key work healthcare professionals do and this shows having being excluded from the 2% payrise, regardless of the being on an AFC contract.

Ban shops from displaying alcoholic drinks by the checkouts, Change the law of how alcohol can be displayed in shops. Vulnerable people are affected by having alcohol displayed so prominently., People's health is at stake. It can affect anyone of any age. Alcohol use is normalised, but causes significant physical and mental harm to many.

Alcoholism is on the increase. There are extensive waiting lists for many alcohol detox centres. Some may never reach this level of help to stop drinking.

Some stores have removed confectionery from checkouts, yet are pushing the sale of alcohol into our view. Cigarettes and tobacco are behind the counters and hidden from display.

Depression, money issues, violence, motor fatalities, relationship breakups, can ALL be fuelled by ALCOHOL.

This ban shouldn’t apply to a specialised wine shop or similar, because it's personal choice to go there.

Improve DWP phone service for PIP claimants and create online portal for PIP, We, the undersigned, are concerned about the challenges faced when contacting the PIP team by phone. Vulnerable individuals, including those with limited mobility or cognitive impairments, endure long waits. Urgent action is needed for timely support and an improved, accessible PIP system., We urge the DWP to address accessibility challenges for vulnerable and disabled individuals accessing the PIP team.
 
We want the Government to:
 
1) Improve Telephone Accessibility: Reduce waiting times, increase staff capacity, and implement a reliable call-back system.
 
2) Establish Online Access: Create a secure portal for PIP services, enabling application submissions, document uploads, case tracking, and easy access to the PIP award letter.

Lower B1 Level English Requirement to A2 Level for Skilled Worker Visa, It's evident that there are staff shortages in many occupations in the UK. However, the high English level requirements for Skilled Worker visa prevents many highly skilled workers from applying for skilled worker visas. It's a barrier talented workers to immigrate to the UK., The Home Office should lower the English requirement level for Skilled Worker visa applications. The requirement for English at B1 Level should be lowered to A2 level. We believe current visa rules are too restrictive, preventing skilled workers from coming to work in the UK, and hurting businesses.

Allow Community First Responders to use green strobe lights on their vehicles, Community First Responders should be permitted to use green strobe lights or rotating beacons to indicate emergency calls and request courtesy. Legislative amendments are necessary to facilitate this., Community First Responders should be allowed to use green strobe lights on their vehicles when traveling to emergencies. These lights would enhance their visibility, alerting other drivers and pedestrians to their urgent mission. This increased awareness can help ensure a faster response time, ultimately saving lives.

The objective is not to demand priority or violate laws but to enhance visibility and signal their response to incidents authorized by Ambulance Service Control.

Launch a Public Inquiry into ongoing HRT shortages in the UK, Since 2018, many women in the UK have been suffering, physically and mentally, due to ongoing HRT shortages. This is despite there being no shortage of HRT in the rest of Europe. This shortage needs to be investigated and addressed, to ensure the wellbeing of women., Hundreds and thousands of women in the UK take HRT, and are facing a health crisis that is not been adequately addressed. This topic needs to be investigated urgently, and new measures taken, such as greater investment into healthcare. We also need to know why some of these medicines (like Utrogestan) are commonly available in Europe but not the UK. We believe the current 2-month limit is not a viable long-term solution.

Ban strobe lighting in public venues to help protect epilepsy, Ban strobe lighting in public venues for health and safety reasons, to protect people with epilepsy. There is no need for strobe lighting, and it can trigger seizures for people with epilepsy. This should help prevent harm to people with epilepsy, and reduce the burden on emergency services., Particularly now there is sound to light to technology, there is no need for strobe lighting to be used, and it should be banned.

Remove planning decisions from local government, Centralise planning decisions to allow central government to take planning decisions that effectively tackle energy security, climate change, housing availability and affordability, inflation and the economy. We believe local authorities often reject planning applications that should be approved., It is time that the interests of the majority are not hindered by local authorities. We believe many local councils are run by NIMBYs who do not support planning applications that are necessary for progress, and that resistance of local government to granting planning permission on greenbelt sites has stifled growth and opportunity.

Ban disposable BBQs to stop wildfires, The Government should ban the sale of disposable BBQs to help prevent wildfires. They can cause huge damage, put a strain on emergency services and put lives at risk. ,

Full legalisation and taxation of cannabis for medical and recreation use, We want the Government to legalise and tax cannabis, following similar models in other countries. Tax revenue to be used directly towards struggling public sectors and other areas in need of funding. Full legalisation could also benefit people with specific and unique medical needs., With the rising cost of living more households and businesses are feeling the pinch. Taxation of UK cannabis would bring in new revenue that would help lessen the effects of the UK's current financial situation. Colorado made over $67 Million in tax revenue during its first year of legalisation. In our current financial climate the potential for millions in additional tax cannot be ignored. It was originally banned throughout the UK in accordance with the 1925 opium convention, a law which is almost 100 years old.

Provide funding for wheelchair accessible equipment in playgrounds
,  
We want the Government to provide funding for at least one piece of equipment in every playground around the country that is wheelchair accessible. So families don't have to travel, as their local playground has something accessible for them.
, I think at least one piece of equipment is a start to a more inclusive country.
 
Currently many disabled children have to pay to go to a wheelchair-friendly playground. While able-bodied children get this for free!!
 
These children never chose to be disabled, this ease of accessibility was cruelly taken from them.
 
This can make disabled children feel excluded and limits exposure of abled-bodied children to our disabled population, which can lead to segregation and lack of equality.

Allow BN(O) holders to use e-gates at passport control, We call upon the UK Government to revise border policies for British National (Overseas) (BN(O)) passport holders. We urge the Government to permit BN(O) passport holders to use e-gates upon arrival., The current policy creates what we believe is an unjust distinction whereby some foreign nationals are allowed to use e-gates, expediting their entry process, but BN(O) passport holders cannot.
 
We believe this disparity contradicts the principles of equality and fairness that the UK upholds. By denying BN(O) passport holders access to e-gates, we believe the Government is undermining the rights and privileges of BN(O) status and also creating a perception of differential treatment among British nationals.

Provide funding to educate the public about sharks , We want people of all ages to be made aware of destructive and unsustainable fishing that has caused a crash in shark numbers across many coral reefs, upsetting the balance of critical marine ecosystems. The Government should provide funding for education in schools and businesses to address this., We want the Government to provide funding to relevant charities to offer workshops and presentations to schools and businesses to develop a better understanding of Sharks the Oceans and the eco system.

Fund free dental care for all, Dental treatment is an essential aspect of healthcare that should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their financial status. Unfortunately, in England, dental treatment is not free for most people and this has led to a situation where many individuals are unable to access the care they need., Thousands of people are suffering from dental problems that could have been prevented or treated if they had access to free dental care. A poll by YouGov of 1,723 adults in England found almost 23 per cent report delaying or going without NHS dental treatment due to the cost. Some 38 per cent of people polled said dentistry should be fully funded by the Government through general taxation, effectively free at the point of delivery.
 
Research has shown that poor oral health can lead to other serious health issues such as heart disease and diabetes. Free dental care could save the NHS money by reducing these issues and other dental issues.

Review and reform the local planning process, We want the Government to review and reform the local planning process, to improve the rights of people who may object to planning applications., We want the planning system to be reviewed and reformed because:
 
1. We believe the consultation process is inadequate
2. We want the public to have a greater role in the process
3. People who object cannot appeal against granting of planning permission

Rollback or reduce the exorbitant hike in IHS and visa fees, Please rollback or reduce the quantum of the exorbitant hike in the Health Surcharge (IHS) for skilled worker visas and students. The increase, from £624 to £1035 per year for workers and from £470 to £776 per year for students, places an overwhelming financial burden on individuals & families, The hike of 65% in IHS fees along with a hike of 15-20% in visa fees makes most sponsored jobs except the very high paying ones economically unsustainable.

For a family of four settling in the UK after 5 years, the total visa fees and IHS would amount to approximately £33,000. This exorbitant sum places an extreme strain on families who are seeking to contribute positively to the UK society and economy.

Allow Skilled Worker Visa holders to get an 'Open Work Visa' after two years, Introduce a new 'Open Work Visa' for people who have worked in the UK for at least two years under a Skilled Worker visa, so they can do any work, without needing a sponsor. This could ease job changes, increase entrepreneurship and make it easier for employers to recruit skilled workers., We believe introducing an 'Open Work Visa' would:
 
- Increase tax revenue by allowing easier job switching and greater competition for high-paying jobs.
 
- Reduce unemployment by enabling skilled workers to create new jobs through entrepreneurship.
 
Currently, Canada and Germany are easing the conditions of work visas and permanent residence, and we believe the employer-dependent work visa for five years to get ILR in the UK is unfair and burdensome.

Don't increase immigration fees for NHS workers, International citizens are a vital part of the NHS workforce. The Government should not increase fees for visas for these workers - which would only make it harder to attract people with vital skills to work in the UK., The Government should appreciate the contribution of international health workers to the NHS, not see them simply as a source of revenue.

Do not increase fees for British National (Overseas) visas, Many British National Oversees (BNO) holders are very disappointed that the Government is planning to increase the visa fees to support the cost for public expenses. , The Government offered BNO visas to Hong Kongers due to political factors and many of us decided to immigrate to the UK for our children's future. 

We don’t have huge funds, and our situation is different to those who are coming here with investment / student/ or working visas. We are working hard for our family's remaining 2.5 years’ visa fees but now we are very worried because the Government wants to increase them even further. Me and many Hong Kongers don’t want to move back!

Increase funding for Mental Health Crisis services,  
We want the Government to urgently increase funding for Mental Health Crisis services. It cannot wait. People are dying.
 
1 in 5 people have suicidal thoughts
1 in 14 people self-harm
1 in 15 people attempt suicide
 
[Source: NHS Digital survey, 2014]
, As a young professional who has considered myself privileged I have had two near miss avoidable suicide attempts. If it wasn't for private healthcare and a supportive employer I would not have been able to navigate the failing service across the NHS. 

I have experienced first hand the inconsistency and lack of support from front line crisis services, as well as being admitted to a private mental health hospital funded by the NHS, which I believe was totally inadequate.

Protect the professional title "sports therapist", Legislate to protect the title "sports therapist", and prevent unqualified people from using this title., The title "sports therapist" is not protected by law, and anyone can call themselves this without having completed a degree in sports therapy. This could have serious consequences because people could be injured, existing injuries could be aggravated, and serious conditions may not be identified (as the person is not formally trained). There is an example of a physiotherapist struck off by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) who continued in practice using the title "sports therapist".

Increase the funding for sand-based/beach sports away from coastal locations, Increase the funding for sand based/beach sport facilities. This includes pitches for beach football/rugby/volleyball and better maintained existing facilities. 

Weather does not limit participation but indoor facility investment would also be a proactive approach., Sand-based sports are a fantastic way to keep fit/healthy and generally improve wellbeing. As someone with recurring knee and joint injuries in my 20's, sand based sports have given me a new lease of active life and are only growing in popularity since the 2012 Olympic Games.

From experience these sports offer lower impact alternatives to regular sports and are not weather dependent. As a regular player of beach volleyball, I have played from January through to December for the last 3 years.

Continue ILR clock when switching between qualifying visas, Switching from one visa that leads to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), like a dependent visa, to another qualifying visa, like a Skilled Worker visa, resets the time needed for ILR. We want this to be changed so the clock for entitlement to ILR is not reset when switching between visas., Current rules can substantially delay when people become eligible for ILR. This can have substantial impacts on families, including eligibility of children to ILR.
 
Resetting accrued ILR can also discourage partners on dependent visas who want to be less reliant on the main visa holder's job or eligibility to stay in the UK.
 
A requirement of 5 years to achieve settlement is understandable. However, the current system means that a person switching visas can already have established ties and ongoing commitments to the UK, but must wait for longer for ILR because of the clock being reset.

Ban putting netting on buildings to deter birds from landing, Ban putting netting on buildings because it can cause death and injury to birds. They can get trapped in and behind the nets and suffer a slow and agonising death. , We believe this should not be legal because it is a form of animal cruelty and shows that some humans believe their aesthetics are more important than an animal's life.

It can also put pressure on services like the fire brigade and charities like the RSPCA when people call them to help with birds trapped in the netting.

Regulate the cost of community sports facilities, Regulate the price of community sports facilities. Many community groups are being financially squeezed when hiring facilities, especially sports venues. For example, some community football groups are unable to afford price hikes and in some cases, venue hire costs between £80 to £120 per match., Many community groups are suffering as a result. Regulation of the cost of community sports facilities should help community groups be able to afford these facilities.

Allow people on skilled worker visas to apply for UK citizenship after 3 years, The essence of a prosperous nation lies in its ability to attract and retain skilled professionals who make an important contribution to the economic, cultural and social fabric of our society. Skilled migrants have historically played a vital role in strengthening our economy., A shorter pathway to citizenship will enhance our nation's appeal to highly skilled professionals, encouraging them to choose the UK as their preferred destination.
Skilled migrants contribute to economic growth through increased productivity, entrepreneurship, and job creation. Accelerating their path to citizenship will enable them to make more substantial long-term investments in our country.
In a globalized world, attracting top talent is a competitive endeavour.

Remove planning permission requirements for boundary walls and gates, The Government should remove requirements for planning permission for boundary structures and provide residents with the autonomy to build robust boundary walls and install gates without a time-consuming planning process. This could help mitigate crime and protect citizens in a quicker way., By removing planning restrictions around boundary walls and gates, citizens can begin to take proactive steps in safeguarding their homes and assets from potential criminals. Enabling the construction of secure boundaries should act as a deterrent against criminal activities and offer a heightened sense of security to residents in their neighbourhoods.

Provide funding to ensure disabled children have access to physical education, I want the Government to give additional funding to mainstream schools to ensure there are enough staff and resources to make sure that every child has access to PE and sports day. Children who have disabilities should be included., Physical exercise is essential in physical and mental health. Particularly in children. Too many disabled children are excluded from PE and sports day. Disabled children shouldn't have to sit on the side line and be excluded. This exclusion can be detrimental to mental health.

Require baby changing facilities in all public toilets, We're urging the Government to enact legislation that mandates there should be baby-changing stations in all men's and women's public toilets, equipped with changing tables, nappy disposal, and sanitation supplies, to cater to the needs of babies and toddlers., The need to include baby-changing facilities in all public toilets is rooted in the principles of gender equality and shared parenting responsibilities. There has been a significant shift in societal norms in recent years, with more fathers actively participating in childcare and taking on equal responsibilities alongside mothers. The lack of baby-changing facilities in men's restrooms creates unnecessary challenges and discomfort for fathers when caring for their children in public spaces.

Create dedicated section for UK passport holders at arrival in UK airports, Have a designated e-gate section for UK passport holders. Nationals from the EU and some other countries can use UK e-gates, whilst British passport holders can't use them in EU countries. We believe this is not fair, and there should be a designated e-gate section for UK passport holders., Currently British passport holders often have to wait in long lines in Europe then again when returning home, due to having to queue in the same line as nationals from other countries, including the EU.

Increase the additional hours that migrants on Skilled Worker Visas can work, The Government should permit migrants on Skilled Worker Visas to work more hours in second jobs than the current limit of 20 hours a week. Ideally, we want the hours to be unrestricted but doubling or otherwise increasing them would be a welcome improvement., Currently, migrants on Skilled Worker Visas are only allowed to work up to 20 hours in second jobs, even if it is in the same occupation code, or on the shortage occupation list. To put this into context, a single night shift can be 12 hours long, meaning two night shifts (24 hours in total) in a week would have already taken one over the 20-hour a week limit imposed by Government. This shows how stringent the current limit is.

Also, there is an abundance of work, especially on the Health and Care sector, as well as an abundance of qualified and willing migrants for said jobs, but unfortunately they cannot take on much of this work because of the 20-hour limit.

Require all education settings provide separate sex toilets from age 4 and up, Require all education settings have separate toilets for boys and girls from reception to university age. Anyone in education should have access to a single-sex toilet. If schools want to provide a unisex toilet that should be additional, not there only option., We believe only providing unisex toilets is a huge safeguarding issue, and can cause significant distress to children who may not be comfortable using these. We want the Government to extend requirements to have single-sex toilets to all educational settings.

Do not introduce new building requirements for separate male and female toilets, We want the Government to scrap plans to require all new non-domestic buildings to provide separate single-sex toilets for women and men and/or a self-contained, private toilet as a minimum: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/new-building-requirements-for-separate-male-and-female-toilets, We believe legal requirements to create single-sex toilets for women and men are unnecessary and discriminatory, and will feed into an ongoing hostile environment towards trans people and put many trans binary and nonbinary and intersex people into situations where we could face violence and hostility for being judged as using the “incorrect” toilet, and also cause trans people without accessibility needs to use accessible toilets for safety, when accessible toilets provision is already inadequate.

Grant home fee status and eligibility for student loans to BNO visa holders, Holders of British National Overseas (BNO) visas and their dependents should be granted home fee status and be able to apply for student loans. , Many don’t realise they face international fee status which means they could pay £20,000 a year. This can hinder those on low-incomes from having equal access to education.

Introduce tax relief for immigration and visa fees, I'm a skilled worker with a foreign passport and have extended my visa four times in the last three years, paying hundreds of pounds of my taxed income to the Government. I believe there should be tax relief for these fees, so tax paid can be reclaimed on immigration and visa fees., Lot of money is paid to the Home office for visa extension or settlement. Current skilled worker application costs £624 to £1423 with an additional health surcharge of £624 for most visa holders. Indefinite leave to remain applications cost £2404 per person. This sum is usually paid from their salary or income that is already taxed. Hence we believe there should be tax relief for these fees, so that tax paid can be claimed back from HMRC.

Seek to rejoin the EU pet passport scheme, The new system of having to go to the vet for an Animal Health Certificate every time I travel to the EU with my pet, and being charged up to £130, is not fit for purpose. The Government should negotiate a deal with the EU so we can rejoin the EU pet passport scheme., The new scheme imposes additional costs on pet owners, which disproportionately affects pet owners on lower incomes more than the wealthy, especially during in this cost of living crisis.
 
Whilst the UK voted for Brexit our pets had no choice.

Require housing for wheelchair users be included in local housing plans, To amend the National Planning Policy Framework to require each Local Planning Authority to set include within local housing plans a policy for a percentage of new homes to be wheelchair accessible. Plans that fail to do so should not be accepted by the Planning Inspectorate., It is estimated that around 400,000 wheelchair users live in unsuitable homes. We want more wheelchair accessible homes built to ensure disabled people can live in homes suitable for their needs; improving their quality of life, independence, opportunities to work and be involved in community life. Without more wheelchair user housing, too many disabled people will be forced to remain in unsuitable homes, impacting their health and wellbeing, as well as creating additional costs for the public sector.

Require planning fees be ringfenced for planning services, Planning is an essential service for the economy and needs support. Under-resourcing of planning services makes the need to ‘ringfence’ planning fees imperative to address a critical issue affecting the sector., Data collated by the DLUHC show the average percentage of all decisions on minor applications made within the statutory time is as low as 46% for 2022-2023, and just 19% for major applications.
 
A lack of resourcing in planning departments has caused both costly and lengthy delays, resulting in uncertainty. The decision not to ringfence the extra income from fees not only risks the proposed changes addressing the issue but risks hindering economic growth. We believe raising planning fees without ringfencing the revenue for planning services will result in continuing under-performance, delay and frustration.

Waive Indefinite Leave to Remain fees for healthcare professionals ,  We petition for a waiver in Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) fees for healthcare professionals, acknowledging their immense dedication in safeguarding public health.
, Our healthcare heroes, including doctors and nurses, deserve recognition. We urge fee waivers to ease their financial burden. The upcoming 20% hike to £2,885 from £2,404 is a heavy burden amidst rising living costs, which affects some healthcare professionals on visas. These individuals play a crucial role in the NHS and our communities. We believe that supporting them financially is an investment in the future of our healthcare system and the well-being of our nation.

Raise the drinking age to 21, Raising the drinking age to 21 could reduce consumption amongst young people because it will be harder to buy alcohol. Also, we believe young people are the group most likely to misuse alcohol; e.g. drinking to excess, which could cause accidents, death and health problems.,

Reconsider the classification of esports, as a sport rather than a game., I would like the Government or Parliament to revisit the classification and recognition of esports in the UK, as currently it is recognised as a game, and not a sport. This hinders the industry as it has meant that there is no national governing body or officially recognised governance., This is dire, as esports not having the level of funding and officiated guidance that sports in the UK have is negatively affecting an industry that even the Department of Digital, Culture, Media & Sport stated has "[the] potential to develop as an area of real national strength in the UK." The recognition of esports as a sport could open the door to more support and help officiate it within the UK, which is nationally, in some cases, decades behind other countries in terms of progress.

Save our sports centres , stop North Lanarkshire closures, Save our sports centres , North Lanarkshire are closing our local sports facilities that help a huge amount  of people keep healthy and support mental health. 

KEIR HARDIE centre has over 250 kids attending football and many other use clubs and other activities weekly, Save our sports centres and community hubs .

Require local authorities to provide public toilets, Public toilets are essential for a healthy and inclusive society. They provide a safe and sanitary place for people to relieve themselves, regardless of their income or social status.

, The lack of public toilets disproportionately affects people who are sick or disabled, the elderly, women, people who work outside, and the homeless. 

However, public toilets are rapidly disappearing in the UK and it is reported that 2,000 public toilets (a third of the total) have closed in England and Wales in the last 20 years.

The Government should make it a legal requirement for local authorities to provide and maintain suitable, safe, clean and appropriately located Public Toilets.

We need to act now to keep public toilets open.

Change the legal drinking age to 16, I think 16 year olds should be allowed to buy alcohol because they can legally leave school at that age and move out, making them a legal adult basically., Change legal drinking age to 16 because 16 year olds can move out and leave school at 16 making them basically a legal adult. Therefore they should be entitled to adult privileges.

Workpermit holder have legal rights to anywhere job if they have legal visa, Give workpermit holder rights to work anywhere with legal, Because sometimes workpermit holder have no work their company and they survived with so many problems and if government approved this so they pay tax and can't do illegal work

Require child-accessible facilities in both public and business-owned toilets, Many public and business-owned toilets are inaccessible to children (e.g. they need to climb or be lifted to reach soap/taps etc). We're asking the Government to require accessible sinks, dryers, soap etc. are provided for kids in these places., Given that children make up a large part of our society, it feels unfair that kids aren't always considered. Regardless of their age, children are people, and therefore have a right to accessible facilities like everyone else. If public and business-owned toilets are required to have features that make facilities accessible to children, we believe it will help all children feel happier, valued and more independent.

Advocate for expansion of visa-free travel worldwide for BN(O) passport holders, The government should actively lobby for expanded global visa-free access for British national (Overseas) passport holders. This includes negotiations with key nations like Vietnam, Indonesia, India, Dominican Republic, Honduras, El Salvador, The United States, and Guyana., We believe advocating for BNO visa-free travel would demonstrate the UK's commitment to British Nationals' rights and acknowledge their contributions. We consider that this advocacy would also serve as a form of soft power, showcasing the UK's global influence. Enhancing mobility for BN(O) passport holders would we believe give the UK a competitive edge in attracting top talent and leaders worldwide.

Seek to develop an international recovery programme for Gaza, We want the Government to work with other nations to enact an initiative to reconstruct Gaza. A major aim of the Marshall Plan was to stop the spread of Communism in Europe. A key aim of this initiative will be to halt the spread of Islamist terrorism., We believe the most important factor in preventing a resurgence of terrorism will be restoring the economy, but that Israel cannot be expected to bear this cost. The Islamist terrorism that struck Israel on 7 October is something which we believe threatens all Western nations. It is in the interest of them all to contribute to a package for Gaza.

The Marshall Plan post-WWII transferred some $13 billion from the USA to Europe for reconstruction. The money played a major role in West Europe’s rapid post-war growth.

Re-introduce Pet Passports, Since the EU departure Pet Passports have been replaced by the Animal Health Certificate or AHC. 
The AHC is an archaic paper system which has to be paid for each trip into Europe., Vets and Pet owners want passports back only certain vet companies want to keep AHCs to make money.
Please make Pet Passports the norm again
Vets have to spend valuable hours completing the pages of the AHC and then charge owners around £200 per animal. Each trip the twenty page document is thrown away after coming back to UK and the whole process starts again.

Ban the captivity of dolphins, whales, and porpoises in England, The last dolphinarium in the UK closed in 1993, but no laws are preventing other facilities from opening. We want to make it illegal to keep dolphins, whales, or porpoises in captivity in England., Dolphins, whales and porpoises are intelligent, social marine mammals. We believe that they are not suited for a life in confinement, which can cause them misery, stress, and extensive suffering.

Although it may be publicly frowned upon, keeping cetaceans captive is not illegal in England, providing an unwanted window of opportunity for the re-emergence of such facilities.

We believe these places should have no future in England. Establishing a ban is the least the Government can do.

Make it compulsory for all dogs to be on leads on public land., Make it illegal to have your dog off a lead in public spaces., Too many dog on dog attacks.
Too many dog on human attacks and deaths.
Too many irresponsible owners with no control over their dog off lead.
No consideration for dogs on a lead who may be nervous of other dogs approaching and traumatised by the experience.
Owners are less likely to pick up dog dirt when off lead.

Provide dedicated funding to support deaf athletes, UK Deaf Sport are asking the Government to end what we believe is discrimination against elite deaf athletes and fund and support them as they do Olympic and Paralympic athletes. This would support elite deaf athletes and the Deaflympics GB Team to compete at the Deaflympics., There is no dedicated funding or Government support for deaf athletes. DCMS provides millions in funding for Olympic and Paralympic Sport through UK Sport each year. Deaf athletes cannot compete in the Paralympics unless they have another Paralympic disability, so deaf athletes are excluded from accessing this funding. Deaf athletes compete in the Deaflympics which precedes the Paralympics. It is an entirely separate event recognised by the IOC as part of the Olympic family alongside the Olympics and Paralympics.

Urgent reforms for fair practical driving test allocations, 1. Ban accounts for driving instructors (ADIs) to book driving tests on behalf of clients
2. Implement a policy where test cancellations are made visible on the website once daily at a specific time, such as 11am.
3.
